help.title: Usage Guide
help.intro: MultiTapKey translates how you press the trigger key (single, double, triple, long press) into the output keys you bind. The trigger key defaults to F24 and can be changed freely; it can come from any device (mouse, keyboard, macro software).
help.section.bind: Use gesture output keys in other software
help.bind.how1_title: Method 1: hold the trigger, then record (recommended for long press / single)
help.bind.how1_step1: 1. Press and hold the trigger key (keep holding it).
help.bind.how1_step2: 2. Open the target app (e.g. a screenshot tool) and start its hotkey recorder — it will ask you to press a key.
help.bind.how1_step3: 3. Wait for MultiTapKey to trigger and emit the output key (the long-press threshold is reached, or releasing registers a single tap) — the app records it.
help.bind.how1_tip: Tip: set the long-press threshold higher (e.g. 3000 ms) so you have time to open the recorder.
help.bind.how2_title: Method 2: press the key on your keyboard (simplest)
help.bind.how2_text: If the output key already exists on your keyboard (e.g. F5), just press that key in the recorder dialog — MultiTapKey is not needed for this step.
help.bind.note: Why not "open the recorder first, then switch back and click the Test button": most recorders cancel as soon as they lose focus; and the trigger key is seen by the target app at the instant it is pressed (a system-level behavior that cannot be intercepted).
help.bind.limit: Double and triple gestures need rapid presses, so they are not suitable for teaching a third-party recorder a hotkey; use long press or single tap for that.
help.settings.trigger: Trigger key: use the "Trigger" button in the binding editor to record a different key — it does not have to be F24.
help.settings.pause: Pause / exit: the app lives in the system tray; closing the window does not quit it. Right-click the tray icon to exit. While paused, all gestures are disabled.
